cases.name: ordered-list-renumbers-after-insert
cases.notes: §3 list rule: an item inserted mid-list renumbers the ordered list from `start` (default 1); the inserted `- ` seed marker is replaced.

cases.name: ordered-list-renumbers-after-move
cases.notes: §3: moving the last item to the front renumbers.

cases.name: tight-list-separator
cases.notes: §3: a list whose raw has no blank line joins its items with `\n`.

cases.name: loose-list-separator
cases.notes: §3: a list whose raw contains `\n\n` joins its items with a blank line.

cases.name: blockquote-rebuild-from-nested-update
cases.notes: §3: the updated paragraph is clean (raw exact); the blockquote whose child changed is rebuilt — children joined by a blank line, `> ` on every line, `>` on the blank one.

cases.name: table-row-update-reinserts-delimiter
cases.notes: §3: rows are rendered and the raw's delimiter row (second line) is re-inserted after the header row.

cases.name: nested-item-update-reindents
cases.notes: §3 render_item: the parent item has a dirty descendant, so its body is its children (paragraph + the sub-list by the list rule) joined by `\n`, then the marker is applied and continuation lines indented by its width.

cases.name: checked-toggles-task
cases.notes: §2.2 attrs: `checked` rewrites the first checkbox — `[ ]`→`[x]` on b_2 and `[x]`→`[ ]` on b_3 — and the list re-renders from its items.

cases.name: checked-on-list-item-without-checkbox
cases.notes: §2.2 + §10 Pinned: `checked` on a `list_item` with no checkbox rewrites nothing and retypes it to `task` in the working tree; the committed re-parse sees the unchanged bytes and stores it as `list_item` again — a new revision with identical content.
